answer: Engineering students may usually count at most two independent studies (no more than 6 credits) as technical elective credits. They need a full-time CE faculty supervisor who approves the credits and reading list and meets periodically; uses include capstone projects, research or a substantial paper.

To register for an engineering independent study: agree with a faculty advisor on content, assessment and timeframe; complete the independent study proposal form; the advisor approves and forwards it to the department chair (or asks for revision); you are notified by email to register after final college approval.

answer: ENGR 597 Independent Study I and ENGR 598 Independent Study II, 3(3,0) each: faculty-supervised research not available in regular courses, ending with a paper or project report; normal drop/withdrawal rules apply. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.

source_quote: The courses offered by the College of Engineering programs are designated according
answer: Engineering course codes follow 'xxxx abc': xxxx = program prefix; a = year/level 1-4; b = program focus area; c = course sequence 0-9. Credit notation c(t,p) gives total, lecture and lab hours (e.g., 3(3,0)).

answer: The College of Engineering Learning Support Center is in room D205, open all week, staffed by graduate and upper-level Teaching Assistants with on-call faculty, and offers books, study guides, course materials, computers, videos and internet-connected PCs.

answer: ENGR 499 My Idea to Innovate (3 credits) is an open course where students with an innovative idea design, with faculty mentors, a cross-disciplinary course once the University Academic Board approves; it can be requested after the first year and can count as technical elective credits.
